pointers.sentence: Asking a callable what it accepts: `django/utils/inspect.py`
`django/utils/inspect.py` answers what Django asks of a function a project hands it: whether it accepts `**kwargs`, what its parameters are called, whether a method takes nothing but its instance.
Django does not use the annotations, the docstring says (`django/utils/inspect.py:signature`).

The docstring of `lazy_annotations` names CPython issue 141560 as fixed in 3.15, and on 3.15 the wrapper passes the format to `inspect.getfullargspec` itself (`django/utils/inspect.py:getfullargspec`).

On 3.14 the wrapper calls it inside `lazy_annotations`, which swaps `inspect._signature_from_callable` for `safe_signature_from_callable`, a `functools.partial` of it adding the format, and back on the way out, under a module-level `threading.Lock` (`django/utils/inspect.py:lazy_annotations`).

Template code calls `getfullargspec`: `Library`'s tag decorators as a tag is registered, and `FilterExpression.args_check`, counting a filter's arguments, as a template is compiled ([Libraries: `Library`, custom tags and `{% load %}`](../templates/libraries.md); `django/template/library.py:Library.simple_tag`, `django/template/base.py:FilterExpression.args_check`).

Template code calls `getfullargspec`: `Library`'s tag decorators as a tag is registered, and `FilterExpression.args_check`, counting a filter's arguments, as a template is compiled ([Libraries: `Library`, custom tags and `{% load %}`](../templates/libraries.md); `django/template/library.py:Library.simple_tag`, `django/template/base.py:FilterExpression.args_check`).

Every question but `is_module_level_function` starts at `_get_callable_parameters`: a bound method is asked as its `__func__` less the first parameter, which its instance fills (`django/utils/inspect.py:_get_callable_parameters`).
`func_supports_parameter` asks whether a name can be passed by keyword; `**kwargs`, which would take it, does not count (`django/utils/inspect.py:func_supports_parameter`).
`method_has_no_args` counts the parameters that are neither `*` nor `**`, and wants none for a bound method and one for anything else (`django/utils/inspect.py:method_has_no_args`).

`is_module_level_function` is true of a Python function whose qualified name holds no `"<locals>"`, which a method of a module-level class, read from the class, also passes (`django/utils/inspect.py:is_module_level_function`).

`Signal.connect` refuses a receiver without `**kwargs` when `settings.DEBUG` is true ([Signals: `Signal`, receivers and sending](../services/signals.md); `django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:Signal.connect`), and `CheckRegistry.register` such a check whatever the setting ([The system checks](../commands/checks.md); `django/core/checks/registry.py:CheckRegistry.register`).

`BaseTaskBackend.validate_task` refuses a task whose function is not module-level, or takes a context but not as its first argument ([Background tasks: `Task`, `TaskResult` and the task backends](../services/tasks.md); `django/tasks/backends/base.py:BaseTaskBackend.validate_task`).

`OperationWriter.serialize` names an operation's positional arguments by `get_func_args` of its `__init__` ([Writing a migration file: `MigrationWriter`](../makemigrations/writer.md); `django/db/migrations/writer.py:OperationWriter.serialize`).

`_get_from_db` warns where an override of `Model.from_db` takes neither fetch_mode nor `**kwargs` ([Deferred fields in a queryset: `defer` and `only`](../querysets/deferred.md); `django/db/models/query.py:_get_from_db`); the admin warns where an override of `ModelAdmin.get_actions` lacks action_location ([Actions: `response_action` and `delete_selected`](../admin/actions.md); `django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._get_actions_with_action_location`).
